entries.reason: get-address must stay a pure vault read: no network (axios), no session cache write, no seed access (getHdCredential). That is a property of the module's whole reachable graph, not of any one call, so no invocation of the command can demonstrate the absence of those imports. Replace with a static import-graph check over the built CLI bundle, which would also cover transitive reintroduction.

On iOS, Android and the extension, main and bg are isolated JS runtimes and hardware resources cross between them as JSON. Reintroducing jpegRgbaUtils or offscreenApiBinaryCodec anywhere on that path breaks the crossing, and absence from a module graph is not observable from any single call. Replace with a static import-graph check over the bg bundle.

thirdPartyDeviceUtils ships in every platform's main bundle, and a runtime import of @onekeyfe/hwk-trezor-adapter would drag in hwk-trezor-core (~620KB). The parity test in the same file imports that SDK on purpose, so the import graph under test cannot be observed from inside this runtime. Replace with a static import-graph check over the main bundle.

The startup baseline ($$debugT0) has to be stamped before the first polyfill is installed, or every timing measured against it is short by the polyfill cost. Importing polyfills/index.ts to observe the order would run the bootstrap under test. Convertible to an AST check: collectTopLevelBootstrapEvents in this same file already orders top-level require and call events and only needs an event for the assignment.
